Rudki Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Rudki's Jewish cemetery was established in the 18th century, when about 30 Jews lived in the town, trading in livestock, lumber, and alcohol; a Hasidic court founded by Pinhas Nasn Safrin (1855–1932) was later seated here, alongside a synagogue of Chortkov Hasidim and two other Hasidic synagogues built before WWI. The ghetto established here in December 1942 saw about 500 people die of hunger and typhus before its April 1943 liquidation, when around 1,700 prisoners were executed; the remaining 300 Jews were expelled to the Janowska concentration camp in Lviv, documented elsewhere in this collection. This is the older of Rudki's Jewish cemeteries, its only dated surviving gravestone from the mid-19th century.
